desc: Ideation: heap-based best-first search over sorted-descending arrays chosen (O(N log N + K log K)); older binary-search/two-pointer plan dropped as O(N²) per check is infeasible.

Implement solve(): fast input, sort descending, heapq with (−value, i, j, k), visited set of encoded ints (i*N + j)*N + k, pop K times pushing up to 3 unvisited neighbors (indices < N), print K-th popped value.
Verify correctness: hand-trace sample 1 (pops 44,38,36,34,31 → answer 31) and sample 2 (all 30000); monotonicity argument (all values ≥ 1) justifies best-first expansion.

Cross-check against brute-force O(N³) reference on small random tests (N ≤ 6, ~5400 comparisons all matched, duplicates and large values covered), edge cases N=1/K=1 and K=N³ verified, sample 3 output 689589940713840351 confirmed.
